text: Ollama Cloud 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Ollama 模型供应商插件，通过注册 ollama-cloud 模型路由和模型发现接入 Ollama API。它会按端点更新并缓存模型目录，依据模型元数据提供思考强度选择，也能使用 Ollama 的网页搜索与网页抓取能力。浏览器侧还可查看账户额度及重置周期。适合希望在 DSH 中使用 Ollama Cloud、切换模型并查看用量的用户。云端功能需要配置 Ollama 凭据；本地或自托管端点可修改地址，且可关闭认证。

Ollama Cloud connects Ollama models to DSH. It discovers models, refreshes the catalog, exposes reasoning levels, and adds web search and page fetching. A browser panel shows account allowance and reset periods. Cloud use needs credentials; local endpoints are configurable.

**Ollama Cloud** 的功能「catalog」：模型目录自动更新：插件查询配置端点的模型列表与详情，将新目录用于模型选择并缓存结果；刷新失败时继续使用当前目录。
**Ollama Cloud** 的功能「reasoning」：模型推理强度：路由按模型目录提供可选思考级别，并将配置的默认级别应用到已解析的模型信息。
**Ollama Cloud** 的功能「web」：网页搜索与抓取：DSH web 能力注册 Ollama 搜索和网页抓取提供方，分别返回搜索来源与提取后的页面文本。
**Ollama Cloud** 的功能「usage」：账户额度面板数据：连接 RPC 通道读取 Ollama balance 响应，解析各计费窗口的剩余额度和重置信息供浏览器展示。
Ollama Cloud 用量与网页功能需要凭据；配置默认引用 OLLAMA_API_KEY，密钥由凭据解析后用于请求。

Ollama Cloud provider for DeepSeek Harness: install it and the provider is configured — with **per-model thinking strength you can actually adjust**.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · dsh-ollama-cloud：Chat runs on Ollama's OpenAI-compatible surface (`https://ollama.com/v1`), model discovery reads Ollama's own native API (`/api/tags`, `/api/show`), and Ollama's web search/fetch endpoints register as harness `ctx.web` providers. The thinking levels each model publishes (off / low / high / max, …) come straight from that model's `thinking` wire metadata, so the composer's Effort selector adjusts real capability instead of a guess.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · dsh-ollama-cloud：The catalog is not frozen at release either. **On every mount the plugin asks the configured endpoint what it serves and adopts the answer for the running session**, then caches it for the next boot; a long-running session refreshes again on an interval. A model Ollama adds, retires, or re-levels therefore reaches you without waiting for a plugin update.

text:
dsh-ollama-cloud README · Usage：1. Pick an `ollama-cloud` model in the composer's model menu (or `/model`).
2. Pick an **effort** in the same menu. The offered levels depend on the model, and the default comes from Ollama's own model metadata.
3. Thinking streams into the transcript like any other provider. The effort is stored per session; a running step keeps the level it started with.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · The catalog: the endpoint is the authority：Ollama adds and retires cloud models on its own schedule, so this plugin does not treat its own release as the model list. Every mount asks the configured endpoint what it serves — `GET /api/tags` for membership, `POST /api/show` for each model's context window, input modalities, and the thinking ladder plus default that model itself declares — and serves that answer. The layers, highest first:
section: The catalog: the endpoint is the authority

text:
dsh-ollama-cloud README · The catalog: the endpoint is the authority：| Layer | What it decides |
| --- | --- |
| Your `models` configuration | per-id overrides, additions, and `enabled: false` retirements |
| The endpoint, just fetched | which models exist, and every capability each one declares |
| The cache of the last fetch | the same answer, read from disk before the network answers |
| The shipped snapshot | display names, and the fallback until some fetch has succeeded |

Two consequences worth knowing:
section: The catalog: the endpoint is the authority

text:
dsh-ollama-cloud README · The catalog: the endpoint is the authority：- **A retired model leaves by itself.** A model the endpoint stops listing disappears, and one its listing still names but answers `404`/`410` for is dropped too — that answer is the endpoint saying its own listing is stale. A detail request that merely *fails* (timeout, 5xx, 429) keeps the model with what the listing said: a slow `/api/show` must not hide a real model for a whole refresh interval.
- **New models arrive with their own levels.** A model the snapshot never shipped keeps its id as the display name until a release gives it a prettier one; its thinking levels are still whatever `/api/show` reports.
section: The catalog: the endpoint is the authority

text: dsh-ollama-cloud README · The catalog: the endpoint is the authority：Models whose metadata is a boolean switch (`kimi-k2.6`, `gemma4:31b`, …) expose Off and High only — on the wire, High means "thinking on". `minimax-m2.7` reports `[true]`, so thinking cannot be switched off and only High is offered. `minimax-m3` reports the thinking capability without a level ladder, so it takes the standard ladder and claims no default; the same applies to any model neither the catalog nor your configuration describes.
section: The catalog: the endpoint is the authority

text:
dsh-ollama-cloud README · Refreshing the catalog：- **At mount** — one refresh as soon as the route is up. The model list is already correct before it lands, because the cache below answers first.
- **On an interval** — `refreshMinutes` later (default `1440`, i.e. daily), and again after each pass. Every pass re-reads the live configuration, so switching the refresh off or changing the interval applies at the next tick instead of requiring a reload; while it is off (or mount-only) the scheduler still ticks every few minutes without touching the network, so switching it back on is honored the same way.
- **The cache** — `<harness home>/cache/dsh-ollama-cloud/catalog.json`, resolved through the harness's own home helper: written atomically, validated on read, ignored when it is malformed or belongs to another endpoint. It lives outside the installed package, so updating the plugin keeps it, and it is what an offline restart — or any restart's first second — is served from.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Refreshing the catalog：Turn the whole thing off with `autoRefresh: false`: the route then serves the cache of the last fetch (or the shipped snapshot before any fetch), and never opens a connection on its own — the honest setting for an air-gapped or quota-limited deployment. `refreshMinutes: 0` keeps the mount refresh and drops the periodic one.

The manual surfaces remain:

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Refreshing the catalog：- **Discover from the endpoint**: any surface calling `llm/discoverModels` lists what the endpoint currently serves, with context windows and input modalities. Only models `/api/show` can fully describe become candidates.
- **Edit by hand**: override `models` in the plugin configuration (below). `enabled: false` hides a shipped model.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Cloud usage in the UI：The plugin ships a browser half that renders in the host's own surfaces — no
separate page, and no provider-UI shell plugin needed:

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Cloud usage in the UI：- **Models page card**: inside the Ollama Cloud row (`Settings → Models`), one
  meter per billing window the plan has, each with its remaining share and reset
  line, the write-only **API key** field, and a refresh button.
- **Sidebar row**: a compact remaining-quota progress bar under the session
  list — the label and percentage on one line, the bar beneath it, filled with
  what is *left* and graded by the remaining share (`ok` / `warn` / `critical`)
  so a shrinking bar reads the same way as the number. Click it for the
  per-window detail; a hover title carries the reset line. It refreshes when the
  sidebar mounts and every 15 minutes after that, and the collapsed 56px rail
  keeps the mini bar plus the percentage with no label.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Cloud usage in the UI：The card reads the account's allowance from `GET <base>/balance` through this
plugin's own host channel (`/ollama-cloud`), so the API key stays on the host
and never reaches the browser. That endpoint reports what is *left* of each
window, and the panel draws the complement; which of its three windows a plan
has is the endpoint's answer, so a plan that reports a monthly one gets a third
meter with no plugin change. A local or self-hosted endpoint answers 404 on
`/balance`; that renders as "this endpoint does not report cloud usage" rather
than an error, and the last good snapshot keeps showing instead of disappearing.
A read that fails transiently (a reset connection, a rate limit, a 5xx from the
endpoint or from something in front of it) is retried once, and a failed row
polls every minute until it recovers, because one bad moment should not leave a
wrong number on screen for a whole cadence. Hover a failure line to see the
machine diagnostic behind it.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Cloud usage in the UI：> The usage channel needs the composition's `connection` row to inject
> `webServer`; this bundle's patch adds that (profiles without a connection row
> skip it). After installing or updating the plugin, restart the harness once —
> until then the card says so itself.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Configuration：Every field is editable from the plugin settings page and overridable per row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: llm-ollama-cloud
  name: 'dsh-ollama-cloud'
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: OLLAMA_API_KEY        # credential reference; empty string = no auth (local servers)

Field semantics:

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Configuration：- `autoRefresh` and `refreshMinutes` control the catalog refresh described above. Both are read live, so a change takes effect at the next scheduled tick — see that section for what "off" still ticks for.
- `models` merges over whatever catalog is in force — the endpoint's live answer, or the shipped snapshot when no fetch has succeeded — and always wins by id, so `enabled: false` retires a model the endpoint still serves.
- `reasoningEfforts` keys are the levels the picker offers (`off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`); values are the spellings sent to Ollama (`off: none`). `false` declares a model with no thinking control; omission inherits the live entry's levels, and an id neither the endpoint nor the entry describes takes the standard ladder (`off`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`max`) with no default claimed.
- `defaultEffort` must be one of the offered levels. It is materialized when a session picks none; otherwise the model's own default applies.
- An override inherits the in-force default level only while it leaves `reasoningEfforts` alone — changing the level set makes the declaration authoritative.
- A declared `defaultE

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Local Ollama / self-hosted endpoints：```yaml
- id: llm-ollama-cloud
  config:
    baseURL: http://localhost:11434/api
    apiKeyEnv: ''                     # a local server needs no bearer token

`baseURL` is normalized: a bare host gains `/api`, a `/v1` spelling maps back to `/api`, and an explicit custom path (`https://gateway.example/ollama`) is kept as written.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Web search and fetch：The plugin registers Ollama's `/api/web_search` and `/api/web_fetch` as `ctx.web` providers — registering changes no deployment policy. To use them:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: ollama-cloud
    fetchProvider: ollama-cloud

Both share the route's credential reference and `baseURL`. Requests carry the credential, so **redirects fail closed**; each attempt has a 15-second budget and one retry on a transient pre-response transport failure.

dsh-ollama-cloud README · Compatibility：- Verified against DSH `0.2.1-rc.1` through `0.2.1-rc.5`. `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.1-rc.1` — the first release whose `connection` row injects `webStartup` — so the `0.2.0` line is outside this release (next bullet). The per-release verdicts live in `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`, and a future regression is recorded in `dsh.compatibility.blocklist`.
- **The bundle patch follows the composition's `connection` row.** `connection.rpc.handle()` mounts a channel through that row's own `webServer` — a caller that injects `webServer` on its own row still throws `cannot get property "webServer" without inject` — so this bundle restates the row's `inject` list with `webServer` added. That list also carries the row's startup dependency, and that one is the composition's to change: the `0.2.0` line injects `webRuntime`, `0.2.1-rc.1` injects `webStartup`. A stale name there does not fail a request; it makes a required row wait forever and fails the whole boot, which is why `pnpm test` compares this patch with the installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` composition (`tests/composition.test.ts`) and `engines.dsh` admits only the releases whose row injects `web
